vision_features.image_context: Close-up photograph of the underside (abaxial surface) of a broad, dark green leaf. The leaf occupies most of the frame, with fine white hairs (trichomes) visible along the midrib, veins, and leaf surface. The background is blurred green, suggesting an outdoor setting. Two leaflets or lobes of the same compound or large simple leaf are visible.
vision_features.abnormalities: 1. Multiple angular to irregular marks distributed across the entire visible leaf surface, concentrated but not limited to areas between veins. Each mark has: a dark brown to nearly black dry central area (approximately 3–15 mm across), surrounded by a bright yellow-green to golden-yellow border zone (approximately 1–3 mm wide), with the outermost edge often transitioning back toward the normal dark green leaf tissue. The marks are angular in shape, suggesting they are bounded by the leaf veins. The central tissue appears dry, slightly sunken or collapsed, and darkened. No powdery or raised surface structures are evident within the marks. 2. Some marks are coalescing along the midrib and major lateral veins, creating larger irregular patches of dark brown dead dry tissue with the same yellow-green halo. 3. Along the leaf margins (edges), there are broader zones of yellowing and darkening following the same pattern, extending inward from the edges in angular patches. 4. The fine white hairs remain intact even over and around the affected areas. 5. The marks are scattered uniformly across the leaf surface with no strong preference for tip, base, or edge exclusively — they appear throughout the interveinal spaces.
vision_features.absences: 1. No powdery white or gray coating is visible on any part of the leaf surface. 2. No raised pustules, blister-like swellings, or orange/rust-colored powdery structures are visible on the underside. 3. No visible insect bodies, frass, eggs, or webbing are present. 4. No water-soaked, greasy, or slimy appearance to the marks — the affected tissue appears dry.
vision_features.summary: The leaf shows numerous angular, vein-bounded marks scattered across its entire surface, each consisting of a dark brown to black dry central area surrounded by a distinct bright yellow-green halo border. The angular geometry of the marks is the most striking feature, strongly following the vein network. The affected tissue in the centers appears dry and collapsed. Nearly the entire visible leaf surface is affected, making the leaf the primary and most severely impacted organ. The sharp yellow-green border contrasting with the nearly black dry central tissue is the single most visually unusual feature.

DISCRIMINATING: 'Bacterial_Blight' vs 'Phytophthora'
Ruling feature : Location of symptoms: leaf lesions with yellow halos (Disease A) vs. dark brown lower stem lesion extending from the taproot (Disease B)
Bacterial_Blight: Small, angular, reddish-brown leaf lesions surrounded by a yellow halo, often coalescing into large dead areas; older lesion centers may fall out, giving leaves a tattered appearance, with symptoms starting in the upper canopy.
Phytophthora: Dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending upward from the taproot, potentially girdling the stem and causing stunting, yellowing, damping off, or plant death.
Decision rule  : IF symptoms are angular, halo-ringed lesions on leaves causing a tattered appearance, THEN diagnose Bacterial Blight (Disease A); IF symptoms are a dark brown lesion on the lower stem/taproot area girdling the stem, THEN diagnose Phytophthora (Disease B).

DISCRIMINATING: 'Bacterial_Blight' vs 'Diaporthe'
Ruling feature : Linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on stems vs. angular leaf lesions with yellow halos
Bacterial_Blight: Small, angular, reddish-brown leaf lesions surrounded by a yellow halo, often coalescing into large dead areas; older lesion centers may fall out, giving leaves a tattered appearance.
Diaporthe: Characteristic linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature stems for pod and stem blight, and sunken gray-brown stem cankers with reddish margins near nodes for stem canker form.
Decision rule  : IF the primary symptoms are angular leaf lesions with distinct yellow halos and tattered leaf appearance, THEN suspect Bacterial Blight; IF the primary symptoms are linear rows of black specks on stems or sunken nodal cankers with reddish margins, THEN suspect Diaporthe.
